# The XOR loop in the binary:
# edx starts at 0xffffffb9
# For each byte at position i:
#   esi = input[i]
#   esi = esi ^ edx  (actually lower 8 bits)
#   compare sil with target_ct[i]
#   edx = edx + ecx (where ecx was the original input byte, not the xored one)
#
# Wait, let me re-read the assembly:
# 0x00401140: add rax, 1
# 0x00401144: add edx, ecx  (ecx is the input byte)
# 
# So the key update is: edx += input[i]
# This means: target_ct[i] = input[i] ^ edx
# And then: edx_new = edx + input[i]
#
# To reverse:
# input[i] = target_ct[i] ^ edx
# edx_new = edx + input[i]

target_ct = bytes([
    0xff, 0xb3, 0x0a, 0xcb, 0xa8, 0x20, 0x8c, 0x98,
    0x3f, 0xcd, 0x02, 0x50, 0xf4, 0x68, 0x09, 0xb6,
    0x3c, 0x8f, 0xdb, 0x7c, 0xea, 0xd9, 0x6f, 0xbc,
    0xbf
])

# edx starts at 0xffffffb9, but we only use the lower 32 bits, and in the comparison
# we use sil which is lower 8 bits
edx = 0xffffffb9

result = []
for i in range(25):
    # input[i] ^ (edx & 0xff) == target_ct[i]
    # So input[i] = target_ct[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)
    inp_byte = target_ct[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)
    result.append(inp_byte)
    # Update edx: edx = edx + input[i] (32-bit wrap)
    edx = (edx + inp_byte) & 0xffffffff

recovered = bytes(result)
print("Recovered input:", recovered)
print("As string:", recovered.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))

# Verify the forward pass
edx = 0xffffffb9
for i in range(25):
    inp_byte = recovered[i]
    xored = inp_byte ^ (edx & 0xff)
    expected = target_ct[i]
    edx = (edx + inp_byte) & 0xffffffff
    print(f"i={i}: input=0x{inp_byte:02x}({chr(inp_byte) if 32<=inp_byte<127 else '?'}), xored=0x{xored:02x}, expected=0x{expected:02x}, match={xored==expected}")

retrieved_cards.title: XOR-then-compare: recover the input by XORing the target back
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A byte-wise XOR with a constant (single-byte, repeating, or position-dependent key) is applied to the input before it is compared against a constant byte sequence.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: XOR is its own inverse; the compared bytes are input XOR key, so the visible target is the encoded form, not the input.

the XOR operand (key) is identifiable or recoverable
